Companion Animal Travel Desk Check-In and Care Rules

This section keeps pet travel moving safely and cleanly at Aurelia Skyways, with fast checks, calm handling, and clear follow-through. Staff must review each booking before the animal reaches the counter, confirm the crate matches the trip, and keep the traveler updated without wasting time. Every animal gets patient attention, and the team treats each handoff as shared responsibility, not a side task.

For small dogs, the crate must fit the approved size standard before acceptance. If the crate is wrong, the agent stops the process, explains the fix in plain words, and records the issue right away. The same goes for loose latches, missing absorbent lining, weak vents, or signs that the animal is distressed. Use the calmest possible tone and keep the lane clear so the next traveler can move without delay. If Hugo Costa or Milan Clark is at the desk, give the same clean guidance and avoid extra chatter. Ruby and any other pet should be handled gently, with steady hands and no sudden movement.

Health papers must be checked before the animal is moved to the holding area. <<FACT F079>> If the document is out of range or unclear, the staff member must pause the handoff and send the case to the senior coordinator. Do not guess, do not waive the step, and do not let pressure from the line change the rule.

If a connection is missed because of a service failure, the case must be logged at once and passed for payout handling. <<FACT F110>> The traveler should get a simple explanation, a written reference, and the next available support step. Keep the note factual and do not debate the outcome at the counter.

When crate condition, documents, and routing all check out, release the animal with a final look over and a short reminder to the traveler. <<FACT F068>> If anything still feels off, stop and escalate at once. Contact the senior coordinator or the duty lead for urgent help.
